I grow cotton, same as always. All 16.1 mu of it. Cotton is what I know, what my neighbors grow, and what the local buyers want. I am not going to change that.

When I first started farming, my father-in-law showed me what to do. After five years I have settled into a routine that works well enough. I do not overthink it. I watch what my neighbors do and I ask the village seed shop owner what seeds are selling well this year.

For seeds, I will buy the improved cotton variety the shop recommends — the same type I bought last year that did decently. I cannot read the technical labels very well but the shopkeeper explains it to me. Hybrid seeds cost more but they grow stronger and I have a large enough household to feed, so I do not want to risk poor yield.

For fertilizer, I apply base fertilizer before planting — mostly compound fertilizer with some urea on top during the growing season. I do it the way my neighbors do: a heavier base application, then topdress when the plants are setting bolls. I probably apply more pesticide than I need to because cotton gets bollworm and aphids badly here and I am afraid of losing the harvest. I spray when I see any sign of trouble.

My well gives me reliable water, so I irrigate several times — before planting to wet the soil, then through flowering and boll setting when the plants are thirsty.

I use rotary tillage. Ploughing deep is hard work and rotary is faster and cheaper to hire the machine for.
